one_liner: Senior protocol officer at Fort Meade planning secure VIP visits, meetings, and events for a cyber command, and drafting command protocol guidance.
fit_summary: Daniel's people skills, policy knowledge, and emergency-management consulting background are relevant, but this GG-13 requires one full year of specialized protocol experience: planning senior-leader events, researching partner customs, and advising protocol staff. It also requires an SCI clearance. Unless Daniel's IEM work included senior-level event and visit planning, Daniel likely won't meet the specialized experience bar.
eligibility: Open to the public, but you must select an employment authority category and upload proof documents for it.
One year of specialized experience in protocol work: planning senior-leadership events and conferences, briefing on partner customs and risks, researching protocol rules, and advising protocol staff.
Experience only; no education substitution is allowed.
Must be able to obtain and keep a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance.
Cyber Excepted Service position under 10 USC 1599f; the two-page resume limit does not apply, and your full resume goes under 'Other Documents'.
strategy: Honestly inventory your IEM work for any time spent planning senior-official meetings, exercises, or conferences, and count the months; you need 12 months matching the four specialized-experience elements.

Frame IEM work in protocol terms where it is accurate: coordinating government-client leadership visits, preparing agendas and briefing materials, and coordinating with partner agencies on requirements.
Because CES is exempt from the two-page cap, use a detailed resume with dates, hours per week, and explicit examples for each of the four specialized-experience elements.
Answer the questionnaire truthfully, since inflated self-ratings can cost you consideration; support every 'expert' answer with resume evidence.
Applications run Oct 27 to Nov 3, 2026, a one-week window. Prepare your resume and eligibility documents ahead of time and submit early.
If you don't qualify, use this posting as a target and pursue GS-9/11 protocol, events, or legislative/intergovernmental affairs roles to build qualifying experience.
resume_bullets: Planned and coordinated [number] meetings/conferences for [senior government client officials] at IEM, assessing [venue, staffing, logistics] resource requirements; [hours/week, dates].
Prepared agendas, action plans, and briefing materials for [client/partner agency] leadership visits, gathering inputs from technical SMEs on [topic].
Researched [partner agency/jurisdiction] requirements and customs and briefed [team size] colleagues on expectations and risks before [engagement/exercise].
interview_questions: Walk us through a high-level visit or event you planned from start to finish. What resources did you identify and what went wrong?
How would you coordinate visitor access to a secured facility with security and access control staff?
How do you research and brief a team on a foreign or external partner's protocol customs?
Describe a time you identified a need for new guidance or procedures and got leadership to endorse it.
watch_outs: Requires an SCI clearance, which means a lengthy investigation and possible delays before you start.
Specialized protocol experience is mandatory with no education substitute, which is a major gap unless your IEM duties match.
On-site only at Fort Meade, MD, with no telework; the commute from Manassas is long.
